properties.citation: Hammarström, Harald, Robert Forkel, Martin Haspelmath and Sebastian Bank. 2026. Glottolog 5.3. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18840967. The 24 living Berber languages with a point (classification under berb1260, level language, not aes-extinct): Awjilah (awji1241), Nafusi (nafu1238), Ghadames (ghad1239), Tetserret (tets1235), Zenaga (zena1248), Tahaggart Tamahaq (taha1241), Kabyle (kaby1243), Tamasheq (tama1365), Tawallammat Tamajaq (tawa1286), Tayart Tamajeq (taya1257), Tachelhit (tach1250), Central Moroccan Berber (cent2194), Tarifiyt-Beni-Iznasen-Eastern Middle Atlas Berber (tari1263), Western Algerian Berber (chen1266), Chaouia of the Aures (tach1249), Siwi (siwi1239), Ghomara (ghom1257), Senhaja De Srair (senh1238), Tunisian-Zuwara Berber (tuni1262), Tidikelt-Tuat Tamazight (tidi1241), Sud Oranais-Gourara (tazn1238), Tumzabt (tumz1238), Ouargli (taga1278), Oued Righ (tema1243).
properties.derivation: Built by social/video/areas.mjs: the union of circles of 1° radius around Glottolog's point for each living Berber language, on Africa's land (Africa's land is the union of the Natural Earth Admin 0 countries whose CONTINENT is Africa); on a 0.05° grid (cells whose centre falls inside), traced back as the cell boundary, simplified by Douglas–Peucker at 0.05° and rounded to 0.01°; parts and holes under 5000 km² dropped. A point is a language's centre, not where it is spoken: the area understates large ranges (Tamasheq has one point for more than 1,000 km), leaves the Arabic-speaking lands between the circles and the diaspora out, and gives no number of speakers. Endangered languages count like large ones.
